**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The MFN in this agreement runs in the right direction. In § 6 (p0047), **TrueLink** covenants that Hosting Services rates "will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party," coupled with a one-year price freeze. That is a Vendor-granted MFN benefiting us — exactly what the rule welcomes, and the detection guidance directs us to mark it compliant and leave it alone.

I confirmed there is no mirror-image obligation on our side:
- **§ 5 COMPENSATION** (p0045) covers only fee schedules, invoicing, and 15-day payment terms — no parity or price-matching covenant.
- **§ 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT** (p0051–p0058) imposes compliance, access-restriction, content and anti-spam obligations — nothing requiring Client to extend TrueLink its best third-party terms.
- Searches for "no less favorable," "most favored," and match/better-terms phrasing returned no further hits.

This sits at the **preferred** position (no MFN obligation on Customer), not merely the fallback.

One observation flagged in the rationale but deliberately *not* redlined: the Vendor MFN has no audit or true-up mechanic, so we would have limited practical means to verify TrueLink is honouring the "no higher than any other party" promise. That is an enhancement opportunity outside this rule's scope — worth raising commercially if you want teeth on it, but it is not a deviation and does not justify opening the clause.
